q: 83. The accuracy in laying down the perpendicular offsets and in measuring them depends upon
explain: The accuracy of perpendicular offsets is influenced by several factors together - the plotting scale, offset length, and importance of the feature being located - so all of these apply.

q: 84. The limiting length of the offset is ... when its perpendicular direction is set out by an eye
explain: When perpendicularity is judged by eye (without instruments), the offset length should be limited to about 15 m to keep errors within acceptable limits for the plotting scale.

q: 85. The instrument used for setting out an offset at a right angle, is called
explain: An open cross-staff is the simplest instrument with two pairs of slits at right angles, used specifically for setting out offsets at 90 degrees to the chain line.

q: 86. The adjustable cross-staff is used for setting out an offset
explain: Unlike the fixed open or french cross-staff, the adjustable cross-staff has a rotatable upper part, allowing offsets to be set out at any desired angle.

q: 87. For setting out an offset at an angle 45, ... cross-staff is used
explain: A french cross-staff has slits set at both 90 degrees and 45 degrees, making it specifically suited for setting out offsets at 45 degrees to the chain line.

q: 88. The relief representation on the map can be depicted
explain: Relief (terrain relief) on a map can be shown using multiple methods - spot levels, altitude tinting/layers, and hill shading - so all of the above apply.

q: 89. Pick up the odd instrument
explain: The dumpy level is the odd one out since it is used for leveling (vertical measurement), whereas the prismatic compass, theodolite, and box sextant are all primarily used for measuring horizontal angles/bearings.

q: 90. For the Abney clinometer the semi-circular arc is graduated as
explain: The Abney clinometer's graduated arc runs from 90 to 0 to 90 degrees, allowing angles of elevation and depression to be read on either side of the horizontal.

q: 91. To use the Abney clinometer as Abney level the vernier should read
options: it is not possible to use clinometer as hand level
explain: To use the Abney clinometer for leveling purposes (as an Abney level), the vernier is set to read 0 degrees, corresponding to the horizontal line of sight.

q: 92. To instrument resembling an alidade is
explain: The tangent clinometer, mounted with a straight edge for sighting and drawing, closely resembles the working principle and construction of an alidade used in plane tabling.

q: 93. Ceylon Ghat tracer can read slopes up to
explain: The Ceylon ghat tracer, designed for locating contour gradients on steep hill roads, can read slope ratios ranging from about 1 in 120 to 1 in 6.

q: 94. The horizon glass of the box sextant is
options: concave in shape to from sharp image
explain: The horizon glass of a box sextant is half silvered (to reflect the image of one object) and half plain/unsilvered (to allow direct view of the other object), enabling angle measurement by superimposing the two images.

q: 95. If the angle between index glass and horizon glasses of a box sextant is 40, the horizontal angle between A and B sight by it is
explain: In a box sextant, the angle measured between the two objects is always twice the angle between the index glass and horizon glass, due to the double reflection principle: 2 x 40 = 80 degrees.

q: 96. An open cross-staff is commonly used for setting out
explain: Since the open cross-staff is a simple, less precise instrument without magnification, it is commonly used only for setting out short offsets where accuracy requirements are modest.

q: 97. The angle of intersection of the horizon glass and index glass in an optical square is
explain: In an optical square, the two mirrors (horizon glass and index glass) are fixed at 45 degrees to each other, causing the incident ray to be deflected through 90 degrees via double reflection.

q: 98. The horizontal glass in an optical square is
options: one-fourth silvered and half un silvered
half silvered and half un silvered
explain: In an optical square, the horizon glass is wholly unsilvered (fully transparent), allowing direct sighting of one object while the other object's image is seen via the silvered index glass reflected through it.

q: 99. The index glass in an optical square is
options: one-fourth silvered and half un silvered
half silvered and half un silvered
explain: The index glass in an optical square is wholly silvered, so it fully reflects the image of the object sighted through it towards the horizon glass.

q: 100. The instrument, belonging to a class of reflecting instrument is
explain: The box sextant works on the principle of double reflection from two mirrors, making it a reflecting instrument, unlike the line ranger or prismatic compass.

q: 101. In an optical square, the angle between the first incident ray and the last reflected ray is
explain: Due to the 45-degree angle between the two mirrors and the principle of double reflection, the optical square deflects the incident ray through exactly 90 degrees.

q: 102. When the object lies on the left hand side of the chain line, then while taking offset with an optical square, it is held in
explain: For an object on the left of the chain line, the optical square is conventionally held in the right hand, upright, to correctly sight and align the offset.

q: 103. The suitable contour interval for a map with scale 1 : 10000 is
explain: For a relatively large scale map such as 1:10000, a fine contour interval of about 2 m is typically suitable to show ground detail adequately.

q: 104. Check lines (or proof lines) in Chain Surveying are essentially required
options: to indicate the accuracy of the survey work
explain: Check lines are measured independently in the field specifically to verify (indicate) the accuracy of the main chain survey framework after plotting.

q: 105. A well conditioned triangle has no angle less than
explain: A well-conditioned triangle in triangulation/chain surveying is one where no angle is less than 30 degrees (and no angle exceeds 120 degrees), minimizing plotting errors.

q: 106. Point of tangency is the
options: common point where the radius changes
common point where the radius and direction changes
explain: The point of tangency is where the circular curve ends and merges back into the straight (forward tangent), i.e., the end of the curve.

q: 107. In a simple curve, 'External distance' is the distance between
options: vertex and middle point of the curve
vertex and the centre of the curve
point of curve and point of tangency
explain: External distance is measured from the point of intersection (vertex) of the two tangents to the midpoint of the curve (the midpoint of the arc), along the bisector of the angle of intersection.

q: 108. An instrument used to find slopes of ground is
explain: A clinometer is specifically designed to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground.

q: 109. An instrument that can be used as an optical square is
explain: A box sextant, when set to read exactly 90 degrees, can be used in place of an optical square to set out right angles.

q: 110. The construction of optical square is based, on the principle of optical
explain: The optical square works on the principle of double reflection from two mirrors set at 45 degrees to each other, deflecting the line of sight through 90 degrees.

q: 111. The surface of zero elevation around the earth, which is slightly irregular and curved, is known as
explain: The geoid is the irregular, curved equipotential surface of the earth that approximates mean sea level and is used as the reference datum of zero elevation.

q: 112. The accuracy of measurement in chain surveying does not depend upon
options: general layout of the chain lines
explain: Overall accuracy of chain survey measurements is affected by offset length, plotting scale, and importance of features, but the general layout of chain lines (while important for framework strength) does not directly affect measurement accuracy in the way the other factors do.

q: 113. The limiting length of an offset does not depend upon
explain: As per the book's answer key, the limiting length of an offset depends on the accuracy required, the method of setting out perpendiculars, and the nature of features surveyed - but not on the scale of plotting.

q: 114. The angle between two plane mirrors of optical square is
explain: The two plane mirrors in an optical square are fixed at exactly 45 degrees to each other to achieve a 90-degree deflection of the line of sight.

q: 115. An angles of 45 with a chain line may be set out with
explain: The french cross-staff has additional slits set at 45 degrees (besides the 90-degree ones), specifically enabling 45-degree offsets to be set out.

q: 116. For taking offsets with an optical square on the right hand side of the chain line, it is held
explain: For an object on the right side of the chain line, the optical square is conventionally held in the right hand, upright, for correct sighting.

q: 117. Correction for pull is
explain: The pull correction to a measured tape length is given by (P-P0)l / AE, where P is the applied pull, P0 the standard pull, l the length, A the cross-sectional area, and E the modulus of elasticity of the tape material.

q: 118. Pick up the most accurate statement from the following
options: survey lines in an area should be as many as possible
number of base lines in an area is limited to one
main chain lines should from well conditioned triangles
oblique offsets are inferior to perpendicular offsets
explain: For accurate chain surveying, the framework of main chain lines should form well-conditioned triangles (angles not less than 30 nor more than 120 degrees), minimizing plotting errors.

q: 119. When a chain line encounters a river
options: chaining is obstructed but ranging is free
ranging is obstructed but chaining is free
both ranging and chaining are obstructed
both ranging and chaining are free
explain: When a chain line crosses a river, physical chaining across the water is obstructed, but ranging (establishing the line of sight/direction) remains possible since both banks are typically visible.

q: 120. Reciprocal ranging is adopted when the following is encountered
explain: Reciprocal ranging is used when the end stations of a chain line are mutually invisible due to intervening obstacles like a river, where surveyors cannot see each other's ranging rods directly.

q: 121. Indirect ranging is adopted when the two ends of chain line are
explain: Indirect (random line) ranging is used specifically when the two end stations of the chain line cannot see each other directly, i.e., they are mutually invisible.

q: 122. A 30 m chain after measuring a distance of 6000 m was found to be 10 cm more than the designated length. If the chain was standardized before the commencement of survey than the true length is
explain: Since the chain elongated during use (became 30.1 m instead of 30 m by the end), the measured length is an underestimate; true length = measured length x (actual chain length/nominal length), giving approximately 6010 m.

q: 123. Let the angular value of one graduation of a tube of length x be theta seconds and R be the radius of its internal curved surface, than
explain: The angular value theta (in seconds) subtended by one division of length x on a bubble tube of radius R is given by theta = x/(206265 R), converting radians to seconds via the constant 206265.

q: 124. Theory of probability is applied to
explain: The theory of probability is applied specifically to accidental (random) errors, since these follow the laws of chance, unlike systematic/cumulative errors which have a definite known cause and sign.

q: 125. Handles are connected to the link by
explain: The handles of a chain are connected to the end links via a swivel joint, which allows the chain to be turned without twisting or kinking the links.

q: 126. To the sum of the first and last ordinates, add twice the sum of the intermediate ordinates. The total sum thus obtained is multiplied by the common distance between the ordinates. One-half of this product gives the required area. This rule of finding the area is called
explain: This is the definition of the trapezoidal rule, which treats the area between consecutive ordinates as a trapezoid, giving area = d[(O1+On)/2 + sum of intermediate ordinates].

q: 127. For high sensitivity of the bubble tube
options: a liquid of low viscosity is used
a liquid of low surface tension is used
the bubble space should be long
explain: A longer bubble space in the level tube increases sensitivity, since the bubble then travels a greater length for a given tilt, making small tilts more noticeable.

q: 128. The following readings correspond to the check at the end of a page of level field book; they are not given in the order. They represent a continuously rising ground: 100.000, 6.000, 0.000, 106.000, 13.000, 7.000
explain: The check involves sum of BS minus sum of FS equal to last RL minus first RL; sorting the given values into BS, FS and RL sets for a continuously rising ground, the correct fourth value works out to 7.000 as per the book's answer key.

q: 129. An imaginary line tangential to the longitudinal curve of the level at the centre of the tube is called
explain: The axis of the level tube is the imaginary line tangential to the longitudinal curve of the bubble tube at its centre (mid-point).

q: 130. An axis about which the telescope can be rotated in a horizontal plane is called
explain: The vertical axis of a theodolite/level is the axis about which the whole instrument (and hence the telescope) rotates in a horizontal plane during swinging.

q: 131. Under ordinary conditions, the precision of a theodolite traverse is affected by
explain: Under ordinary field conditions, systematic linear errors (such as those from a mis-calibrated tape) most significantly affect the precision of a theodolite traverse, since they accumulate consistently rather than cancel out.

q: 132. The approximate formula for radial or perpendicular offsets from the tangent, is
explain: As per the book's answer key, the approximate offset formula from the tangent to the curve is given as x/R, used for small offsets in curve setting out.

q: 133. A chain may get elongated due to
explain: A chain elongates mainly due to the opening out (wear and stretching) of the connecting rings between links over repeated use, per the book's answer key, though temperature and pull can also contribute.

q: 134. A chain is made up mild steel or galvanized iron wire of diameter
explain: A standard surveying chain is made of mild steel or galvanized iron wire of about 4 mm diameter.

q: 135. Handles of chains are made up of
explain: As per the book's answer key, chain handles are listed as being made of copper (though brass is more commonly cited in general surveying texts; this answer follows the printed key).

q: 136. In precision theodolite traverse for roads and railways, the angular error of closure should not exceed
explain: For precision theodolite traverses used in road/railway alignment, the permissible angular error of closure is taken as 30 seconds multiplied by the square root of the number of stations (N).

q: 137. The projection of a traverse line on a line perpendicular to the meridian is known as
explain: As per the book's printed answer key, this projection (onto a line perpendicular to the meridian) is designated as the latitude of the line in this text, though standard convention typically calls this the departure - readers should verify against their copy.

q: 138. The projection of a traverse line on a line parallel to the meridian is known as ... of the line
explain: As per the book's printed answer key, this projection (onto a line parallel to the meridian) is designated departure in this text, though standard convention typically calls this the latitude - readers should verify against their copy.

q: 139. A negative declination shows that the magnetic meridian is to the
options: eastern side of the true meridian
western side of the true meridian
explain: A negative (west-negative convention) declination indicates the magnetic meridian lies to the eastern side of the true meridian, as per the book's sign convention.

q: 140. Agate cap is fitted with
explain: An agate cap, which reduces friction at the pivot point, is a component fitted in a spirit level's bubble tube mounting mechanism.

q: 141. The process of turning the telescope about the vertical axis in horizontal plane is known as
explain: Rotating the telescope about the vertical axis in a horizontal plane (left or right) is called swinging the telescope.

q: 142. For which of the following permanent adjustments of theodolite, the spire test is used?
options: Adjustment of altitude bubble and vertical index frame
explain: The spire test is used to check and adjust the horizontal (trunnion) axis of a theodolite, ensuring it is truly perpendicular to the vertical axis, by sighting a high point in both faces.

q: 143. Which of the following methods of contouring is most suitable for hilly terrain?
explain: The tacheometric method of contouring is most suitable for hilly terrain because it quickly provides both horizontal distance and elevation to numerous points without the need for chaining across difficult ground.

q: 144. An invar tape is generally used for accurate measurement of distance because it possesses ... coefficient of thermal expansion
explain: Invar (a nickel-steel alloy) has a very low coefficient of thermal expansion, making tapes made from it far less sensitive to temperature-induced length changes, ideal for precise base line measurement.

q: 145. The instrument attached to the wheel of a vehicle in order to measure the distance travelled, is called
explain: An odometer is fitted to a vehicle's wheel to measure the total distance travelled by counting wheel rotations.

q: 146. It is more convenient and gives better results while measuring horizontal distance ... by stepping method
explain: Stepping method for measuring horizontal distance on sloping ground gives better, more convenient results when done downhill, since gravity assists in maintaining a horizontal tape segment.

q: 147. Direct ranging is possible only when the end stations are
options: located at highest points in the sea
explain: Direct ranging (surveyor at one end directing the other by signals) is possible only when the two end stations of the line are mutually intervisible.

q: 148. The error in measured length due to incorrect holding of chain is
explain: An error caused by incorrect holding/application of the chain (a fault attributable to the physical instrument's use) is classified as an instrumental error in this context.

q: 149. In reciprocal leveling, the error which is not completely eliminated, is due to
explain: Reciprocal leveling eliminates errors due to curvature, refraction, and non-adjustment of the line of collimation when readings from both ends are symmetric, but a small residual error due to non-adjustment of the line of collimation may remain if refraction is not identical at both setups.

q: 150. For true difference in elevations between two points A and B, the level must be set up
options: at any point between A and B
at the exact midpoint of A and B
explain: As per the book's answer key, for practical single-setup leveling the instrument is set up near point A (one end), though the theoretically ideal position to cancel curvature/refraction errors is the exact midpoint.

q: 151. The most commonly used set of theodolite operations are
explain: As per the book's answer key, the most commonly used operational combination is right face and right swing.

q: 152. Geodetic surveying is different from plane surveying because of
options: the large difference of elevations between various points
explain: Geodetic surveying differs fundamentally from plane surveying because it covers very large areas where the curvature of the earth cannot be ignored, requiring spherical (geodetic) rather than plane computations.

q: 153. The error due to bad ranging is
explain: As per the book's answer key, the error due to bad ranging (random deviations from the true line) is treated as a compensating error, tending to partially cancel out over a series of measurements.

q: 154. Offsets are
options: ties or check lines which are perpendicular to chain line
sets of minor instruments in chain surveying
chain lines which go out of alignment
explain: Offsets are lateral (typically short) measurements or ties, often perpendicular, taken from the chain line to locate the position of nearby details/objects.

q: 155. The tension, at which the effects of pull and sag for a tape are neutralised, is known as
explain: Normal tension is the specific value of pull at which the tape's elongation due to increased pull exactly balances the shortening effect due to reduced sag, neutralizing both effects.

q: 156. A line joining the apex of a triangle to some fixed point on the opposite side is called a
explain: As per the book's answer key, a line joining the apex of a triangle to a fixed point on the opposite side is termed a base line in this context.

q: 157. The included angles of a theodolite traverse, are generally measured
explain: As per the book's answer key, included angles in a theodolite traverse are generally measured anti-clockwise from the forward station.

q: 158. Distance between two neighboring brass rings is
explain: In a standard surveying chain, brass rings (tally markers) are typically placed at every 20 cm interval (metre marks) to allow easy identification of sub-divisions.

q: 159. When the image formed by the objective is not situated in the plane of cross-hairs
explain: As per the book's answer key, when the image is not in the plane of cross-hairs, the cross-hairs (diaphragm) themselves should be adjusted to correctly coincide with the image plane.

q: 160. When 1 cm on a map represents 10 m on the ground, the representative fraction of the scale is
explain: 1 cm = 10 m = 1000 cm, so the representative fraction is 1:1000, i.e., 1/1000.

q: 161. The representative fraction 1/2500 means that the scale is
explain: RF of 1/2500 means 1 cm on the map represents 2500 cm on the ground, which equals 25 m.

q: 162. The main object of running a tie line is
options: to check accuracy of the work
to take details of nearby objects
to take offsets for detailed surveying
explain: The primary purpose of a tie line is to take offsets for detailed surveying of interior details that are located far from the main chain lines.

q: 163. The main difference between an optical square and prism square is
options: that optical square is more accurate than prism square
that no adjustment is required in a prism square since the angle between the reflecting surfaces cannot be changed
explain: The key difference is that a prism square, being a single solid glass prism with a fixed 90-degree angle between reflecting surfaces, requires no adjustment, unlike an optical square with separate adjustable mirrors.

q: 164. Rankine's deflection angle in minutes is obtained by multiplying the length of the chord by
options: square of the degree of the curve
inverse of the degree of the curve
explain: Rankine's method computes the deflection angle (in minutes) for setting out a curve by multiplying the chord length by the degree of the curve, using a simplified tangential angle formula.
